research.question: Is a single load-more control at the end of a mobile list, with the loaded rows kept, a recognised pattern, and what does the evidence say about end and loading signals?
research.reason: The brief asks whether a novice reads that the list went on; PD-1 leans on convention.

sources.title: Infinite Scrolling, Pagination Or 'Load More' Buttons? Usability Findings In eCommerce (Baymard Institute)
sources.claim: A load-more button at the end of the list with the loaded items staying solved the usability issues seen with pagination; for mobile, one large button after about 15-30 items; never infinite scroll for search results.

research.summary: The pattern and page size are supported; nothing on busy or end signals.

decisions.summary: F1: the first new row takes focus (MmListRow autoFocus) and a visually hidden polite status says how many rows joined and whether every match is listed.
decisions.authority: chair, under WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.3 and 2.4.3 as the guard cited

decisions.summary: F2/PD-3: the packs are asked for one more than the page; the offer shows only while there are more, so exactly a page never offers more and the silent end cannot occur. PD-3's caption is therefore not drawn.
F4: a test for 'A new query starts over', and one for exactly a page.
PD-1/F5: the text kind stays; MM-410's Decisions say the Ember word marks the continuation and the outline the exit.
PD-2/F3 (loading): no spinner; the read is local and measured at 16 ms on a laptop (MM-51); the phone measurement is the owner's (Q2). Built only if perceptible.
F3 (failure): a proposed ticket, MM-411, a failed page of results says so; not built with MM-410 (useAsync swallows errors; rare on local SQLite).
PD-4: 'More results' stays; 'More foods' is the owner's call (Q1).
PD-5: the rows' padding inside the padded sheet, pre-existing, needs a render (Q3).
